title: Prove session completion reporting in Node Vitest

intentCoverage.report:
Dough Intent Coverage: SEED-413#prove-session-completion-reporting-on-vitest at 9e1e7d15037805f4d520ed3f19f658f7b239c756 (branch claude/prove-session-completion-reporting-in-node-vites).

Verdict: Caught.

Promise: a completion report refused as cross-site keeps the earlier completion message (story scope: "delivery identity, duplicates and refusals"; spec header: "A completion report refused for another launch, or as malformed or cross-site, keeps the message ... recorded earlier").

Fault: dashboard/server/completionAdmission.ts `admitCompletionRequest` with the `verifySameOrigin(request.origin, request.host, request.fetchSite);` line replaced by a comment (cross-site origin check skipped). Fixtures and assertions untouched.

Target choice (revision of the suggestion): the suggested alternative fault, skipping `knownSource(...)`, was not used. Reading deliverCompletion shows an unknown source still reaches `reportingAttempt`, which refuses a source that does not match the kept attempt with the same 404. So that fault would most likely leave the promised behavior unchanged and could not support a verdict. Skipping `verifySameOrigin` does change behavior on the path the maintained spec exercises: its fetch stub (dashboard/backend-tests/support/installedPublisher.ts) sends every request through production `admitCompletionRequest` and then `deliverCompletion`. In production the HTTP adapter `submitCompletion` also calls `verifyLocalOrigin(req)` first, so this result is limited to the admission function and the reporting script's fetch-bridge path. The quiet-closure alternative was not probed.

Maintained check examined: dashboard/backend-tests/sessions/agent-completion-refusals.spec.ts "refused deliveries keep the earlier completion message".

Command (scratch checkout, detached worktree at the selected revision, deps via `node scripts/setup-native.mjs npm` exit 0, Node 24.21.0 matching .node-version):
env -u NO_COLOR -u FORCE_COLOR -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES -u OPEN_DOUGH_DASHBOARD_BACKEND_SPLIT npm run --silent test:dashboard:backend -- 'sessions/agent-completion-refusals\.spec\.ts$' --workers=1

Observations:
- Baseline: clean scratch state (`git status --porcelain` empty). 1 test passed and ran the refusal case (exit 0).
- Faulted: exit 1. The test failed at the refusal-status assertion in the loop, agent-completion-refusals.spec.ts:114, `expect((await refused({ ...valid, ...change }, from)).status).toBe(status)`, for the cross-site row `[{}, "https://elsewhere.test", 403]`: "expected 200 to be 403". The cross-site report was accepted.
- Independent wrong-behavior witness: a temporary scratch copy of the spec (ic-witness.spec.ts, same setup, one cross-site POST, no refusal assertions) ran under the fault. It logged status 200 and a kept completion of outcome "unfinished", message "Required retirement is held; resolve ownership.", replacing the earlier "completed" / "Publication finished. Reminder: inspect the migration." So the promised behavior did go wrong on the exercised path: the cross-site report was admitted and overwrote the earlier message. The maintained spec caught this on the status before its following kept-message assertion ran.
- Recognition: no already-planned repair or prior disposition matches. The probe raises no new repair decision.

Next proof action: none needed for this promise on this path. The maintained refusal-status assertion catches the cross-site fault.

Restoration: an EXIT trap ran `git checkout -- dashboard/server/completionAdmission.ts` and removed the witness spec. Afterwards `git status --porcelain` and `git diff` were empty and HEAD was still 9e1e7d15037805f4d520ed3f19f658f7b239c756. The same command was rerun and passed (exit 0, 1 test). The scratch worktree was then removed with `git worktree remove --force` (exit 0). `git worktree list` no longer shows it, the directory is gone, and the execution checkout status is still clean.

Costs:
- Test runtime (measured, Vitest-reported Duration per run): baseline 1.15s, faulted 0.567s, witness 0.469s, restored 0.498s. Total about 2.7s of runner time. Dependency setup time was not measured separately.
- Human effort: unavailable. No human took part in this probe and there is no separate measure.
- Agent effort: unavailable. No separately supported token or tool-time measure is available to this agent.
- Invocation-to-report elapsed: 84974 ms.

Wrap-up disposition: checked revision 9e1e7d15037805f4d520ed3f19f658f7b239c756, verdict Caught, no follow-up.
